subject: Why is occurrence function taking long time and have not yet to produce results?

messages.author: cb97dd721185ed40
messages.subject: Why is occurrence function taking long time and have not yet to produce results?
parts:
I am only using first 500 data points consisting of animal GPS coordinates and DOP values which is put in an telemetry object.  Also keep in mind that the data was irregularly sampled (contisting of several cycles of 5min, 30min, and 4hr intervals). I created a model which was fitted via variogram.fit() then ctmm.fit().  However when I run the model using occurence function, it seem to taking too long, taking around 30 hours until I decided to stop it.

Any tips on how to shorten that processing time?  Here's the code that I was using:

# Convert time to POSIXct objects
LHdata[,timestamp := as.POSIXct(LMTdatetime.GPS.rounded, tz=timezone)]


# telemetry assumes Movebank naming conventions.
# Sufficient MoveBank columns include:
#
#   individual.local.identifier
#   timestamp
#   location.long
#   location.lat
#
# If DOP values are to be included, the column name should be "GPS.DOP"
LHdata[,individual.local.identifier := UNIQUE_ID]
LHdata[,location.long := Longitude]
LHdata[,location.lat := Latitude]
LHdata[,GPS.DOP := DOP]
LHtele <- as.telemetry(
  object = LHdata,
  timezone = timezone
)


# Create and fit a variogram model (which should be stored in GUESS)
SVF2 <- variogram(LHtele,dt=dt)
variogram.fit(SVF2)


# Fit a ctmm model.
FIT2 <- ctmm.select(data = LHtele, CTMM = GUESS)


# Compute occurrence distribution
UD <- occurrence(LHtele,FIT2)  # This one seem to be taking forever

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Why is occurrence function taking long time and have not yet to produce results?
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I suspect its the gaps. Occurrence distributions of all types are very sensitive to large gaps in the data. Large gaps take longer to fill in (computationally) and even then they just produce a big blob because you don't know where the animal was during the gap. So the output would not look good even if you waited for the calculation to finish. There are two arguments in occurrence() to skip gaps: dt.max and cor.min:

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/occurrence.html

I was going to type some recommendations for reasonable arguments, but I just went ahead and updated the development version of the package on GitHub to have more better/tighter default arguments. You can upgrade via:

devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm")

Please see if that helps.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 343fd12501b7fca4
messages.subject: Re: Why is occurrence function taking long time and have not yet to produce results?
parts:
Hi Chris,

I'll just hop on here because I have a similar issue. I have some large gaps (days long) in my data due to Iridium issues. This causes my AKDE estimates to balloon up. I just saw your above post and learned about the dt.max argument, so I figured I would try it out to get seasonal UDs for my bobcats from which I could create 95% UD polygons. I set dt.max at 5 hours (in seconds) for our collars which are on 4 hour fix rates.

ud <- occurrence(data,top.mod,dt.max=5*3600)

For some reason the ud still appears blown up, and when I try to summarize the area of the ud, I get this message.

occurrence area is not generally meaningful, biologically.

Any thoughts on why the UD is still huge? Is there a similar dt.max argument for the akde function, so I could use that to get seasonal home ranges?

Thanks,
Dave

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Why is occurrence function taking long time and have not yet to produce results?
parts:
Hi Dave,

The output of occurence() is not an AKDE. You want akde() for home-range estimation. I don't return occurrence areas with summary() because they are commonly misreported as home-range areas.

  • C. H. Fleming, W. F. Fagan, T. Mueller, K. A. Olson, P. Leimgruber, J. M. Calabrese, "Rigorous home-range estimation with movement data: A new autocorrelated kernel-density estimator", Ecology 96:5, 1182-1188 (2015)
  • C. H. Fleming, W. F. Fagan, T. Mueller, K. A. Olson, P. Leimgruber, J. M. Calabrese, "Estimating where and how animals travel: An optimal framework for path reconstruction from autocorrelated tracking data", Ecology 97:3, 576-582 (2016)

If I had to guess why your occurrence distributions are blown up, its probably because the bobcats get around quite a bit within 4 hours. What were the autocorrelation parameters estimated to be?

AKDE doesn't need a dt.max argument, but may benefit from the weights argument when sampling is irregular.

  • C. H. Fleming, D. Sheldon, W. F. Fagan, P. Leimgruber, T. Mueller, D. Nandintsetseg, M. J. Noonan, K. A. Olson, E. Setyawan, A. Sianipar, J. M. Calabrese, "Correcting for missing and irregular data in home-range estimation", Ecological Applications 28:4, 1003-1010 (2018)

Best,
Chris
